terms.definition: Relational Database Service — AWS's fully managed platform for running relational databases without managing servers, OS, or DBMS software yourself
terms.example: Like hiring a professional DBA who handles all maintenance so you can focus on your application

terms.definition: Multi-Availability Zone — a high-availability feature that maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ for automatic failover
terms.example: If your primary database's data center goes down, AWS automatically promotes the standby in another data center in under 120 seconds

terms.definition: An asynchronously replicated, read-only copy of the primary RDS database used to scale read traffic
terms.example: Your analytics dashboard reads from the replica while your application writes to the primary — neither slows the other down

terms.definition: AWS's cloud-native MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible database engine, offering 3-5x better performance than standard engines with distributed storage
terms.example: Like taking a regular car engine and rebuilding it specifically for a racetrack — same fuel (SQL), but much faster

terms.definition: A replication method where a write is only confirmed after both the primary and the standby have written the data — used by Multi-AZ
terms.example: Like getting a signed receipt from both parties before a transaction is considered complete

terms.definition: A replication method where the primary confirms writes immediately, and the replica catches up shortly after — used by Read Replicas
terms.example: Like sending a letter — you can continue your day once you mail it, even though it hasn't arrived yet

terms.definition: The delay between a write on the primary database and when that change appears on the Read Replica due to asynchronous replication
terms.example: If you write a record and immediately query the replica, you might not see it yet — it arrives in milliseconds, but not instantly

terms.definition: Online Transaction Processing — database workload pattern involving many small, fast read/write operations typical of live applications
terms.example: Every time a customer places an order or updates their profile — thousands of small operations per second

terms.definition: Online Analytical Processing — database workload pattern involving complex queries that scan large amounts of historical data for analysis and reporting
terms.example: Running a quarterly report that aggregates millions of transactions by region, product, and customer demographics

terms.definition: AWS's fully managed petabyte-scale data warehouse service designed for OLAP workloads using MPP and columnar storage
terms.example: Like a giant research library where instead of one librarian reading every book, 100 librarians work in parallel to find your answer

terms.definition: Massively Parallel Processing — Redshift's architecture that breaks large queries into pieces and executes them simultaneously across many compute nodes
terms.example: Instead of one person reading 10,000 pages, 100 people each read 100 pages simultaneously then combine their findings

terms.definition: A storage method where each database column is stored separately on disk, allowing queries to read only the needed columns — dramatically reducing I/O for analytics
terms.example: Instead of a filing cabinet with full employee folders, imagine separate drawers: one for all names, one for all salaries — analyzing salaries means opening only the salary drawer

terms.definition: A Redshift feature that allows running SQL queries directly against data stored in Amazon S3 without loading it into Redshift first
terms.example: Query 5 years of historical log data sitting in S3 without paying to store it all in Redshift's compute nodes

terms.definition: AWS's fully managed in-memory caching service supporting Redis and Memcached, used to reduce database load and speed up application reads
terms.example: Like a sticky note on your desk — instead of going to the filing cabinet every time, you check the note first

terms.definition: When the requested data is found in ElastiCache (RAM), allowing it to be returned instantly without querying the database
terms.example: You ask for the homepage content, ElastiCache has it — returned in microseconds, database untouched

terms.definition: When requested data is NOT in ElastiCache, requiring the application to fetch it from the database, store it in cache, then return it
terms.example: First visitor of the day triggers a DB query — but the 1,000 visitors after them all get the cached version instantly

terms.definition: An open-source in-memory data structure store used as a cache, session store, and message broker — supports persistence, replication, and complex data types
terms.example: Not just key-value pairs — Redis can store sorted sets (leaderboards), lists (queues), hashes (objects), and more, with automatic backup

terms.definition: A simpler in-memory key-value cache engine, fast and horizontally scalable but lacking persistence, replication, and complex data structures
terms.example: Great for a simple 'store this string, get this string' cache where you don't care if data is lost on restart

terms.definition: Time To Live — a setting that automatically expires and removes cached data after a specified duration, preventing stale data from being served indefinitely
terms.example: Cache product prices for 5 minutes (TTL=300 seconds) — after that, ElastiCache fetches fresh prices from the database automatically

terms.definition: Database Migration Service — AWS service that migrates databases to AWS quickly with minimal downtime, keeping the source operational during migration
terms.example: Move your on-premises MySQL to RDS without taking your application offline for days

terms.definition: A DMS migration where the source and target databases use the same engine (e.g., MySQL to MySQL, Oracle to Oracle)
terms.example: Moving a self-managed MySQL on EC2 to a fully managed RDS MySQL — same engine, just different hosting

terms.definition: A DMS migration where the source and target databases use different engines (e.g., Oracle to PostgreSQL), requiring schema conversion using SCT
terms.example: Moving from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL — different SQL dialects, different stored procedure syntax, requires schema conversion first

terms.definition: Schema Conversion Tool — an AWS tool that automatically converts database schemas and stored procedures from one engine format to another for heterogeneous migrations
terms.example: Translating an Oracle PL/SQL stored procedure into PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL syntax automatically

terms.definition: The combination of CPU, memory, and network capacity allocated to an RDS database instance, similar to EC2 instance types
terms.example: db.t3.micro (small, burstable — great for dev/test), db.m5.large (general purpose production), db.r5.2xlarge (memory-optimized for large databases)
